questions.q: Which of the following statements regarding the Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP) is/are correct? 1️⃣ The idea was borrowed from the Irish Constitution of 1937. 2️⃣ Dr. B.R. Ambedkar described them as the 'conscience of the Constitution'. 3️⃣ They are enumerated in Part IV of the Constitution from Articles 36 to 51.
questions.e: Statement 1 and 3 are correct as the idea was borrowed from the Irish Constitution and they are in Part IV, Articles 36-51. Statement 2 is incorrect because Dr. B.R. Ambedkar described them as 'novel features' , while Granville Austin described the Fundamental Rights and Directive Principles together as the 'Conscience of the Constitution'.

questions.q: With reference to the nature of Directive Principles of State Policy, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ They are constitutional instructions or recommendations to the State in legislative, executive, and administrative matters. 2️⃣ They are justiciable in nature and enforceable by the courts for their violation. 3️⃣ They aim at establishing social and economic democracy in the country.
questions.e: Statement 1 and 3 are correct as these principles are instructions to the State and aim to establish social and economic democracy. Statement 2 is incorrect because the Directive Principles are non-justiciable, meaning they are not legally enforceable by the courts for their violation.

questions.q: According to Article 37 of the Indian Constitution, the Directive Principles are: 1️⃣ Fundamental in the governance of the country. 2️⃣ The duty of the State to apply in making laws. 3️⃣ Primarily enforced through the moral force of public opinion.
questions.e: All statements are correct. Article 37 makes these principles fundamental in governance and mandates the State to apply them. Since they are non-justiciable, the real force behind them is political, which is the moral force of public opinion.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes the classification of Directive Principles of State Policy in the Constitution?
o: The Constitution does not contain any classification.
questions.e: The Constitution does not contain any formal classification of the Directive Principles. However, on the basis of their content and direction, they are usually classified into three broad categories: Socialistic, Gandhian, and Liberal-Intellectual.

questions.q: Which of the following Directive Principles are based on the ideology of Socialism? 1️⃣ Article 38 (Promotion of welfare of people). 2️⃣ Article 40 (Organization of village panchayats). 3️⃣ Article 41 (Right to work and education). 4️⃣ Article 43 (Living wage and decent standard of life).
questions.e: Articles 38, 41, and 43 are Socialistic principles aiming to provide social and economic justice. Article 40 (Organization of village panchayats) is a Gandhian principle.

questions.q: Consider the following statements regarding Article 38 of the Directive Principles: 1️⃣ It directs the State to secure a social order for the promotion of welfare of the people. 2️⃣ It seeks to minimize inequalities in income, status, facilities, and opportunities. 3️⃣ The provision to minimize inequalities was added by the 42nd Amendment Act of 1976.
questions.e: Statement 1 and 2 are correct as Article 38 aims for a social order that minimizes inequalities. Statement 3 is incorrect because the provision to minimize inequalities in income, status, etc., was added by the 44th Amendment Act of 1978, not the 42nd.

questions.q: Under Article 39, the State is directed to secure which of the following? 1️⃣ Equal pay for equal work for both men and women. 2️⃣ Prevention of concentration of wealth and means of production. 3️⃣ Protection of the health and strength of workers and children. 4️⃣ Right to an adequate means of livelihood for all citizens.
questions.e: All four points are explicitly mentioned as directives under Article 39 to promote socialistic goals.

questions.q: With reference to the 'Gandhian Principles' in DPSP, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ They represent the programme of reconstruction enunciated by Gandhi during the national movement. 2️⃣ They include the promotion of cottage industries on an individual or co-operative basis in rural areas. 3️⃣ They direct the State to organize agriculture and animal husbandry on modern and scientific lines.
questions.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct as Gandhian principles focus on rural reconstruction and cottage industries (Article 43). Statement 3 is incorrect because organizing agriculture on modern and scientific lines (Article 48) is categorized as a Liberal-Intellectual principle.

questions.q: Which of the following Articles directs the State to "promote the educational and economic interests of SCs, STs, and other weaker sections"?
questions.e: Article 46 directs the State to promote the educational and economic interests of Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, and other weaker sections and to protect them from social injustice.

questions.q: Consider the following statements regarding Article 44: 1️⃣ It directs the State to secure for all citizens a uniform civil code throughout the territory of India. 2️⃣ It is classified as a Liberal-Intellectual principle. 3️⃣ It was added to the Constitution by the 42nd Amendment Act of 1976.
questions.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct as Article 44 deals with the Uniform Civil Code and falls under the Liberal-Intellectual category. Statement 3 is incorrect because Article 44 was part of the original Constitution.

questions.q: Which of the following Articles was amended by the 86th Amendment Act of 2002?
questions.e: The 86th Amendment Act of 2002 changed the subject matter of Article 45, making elementary education a Fundamental Right under Article 21A, while Article 45 now directs the State to provide early childhood care and education for all children until they complete the age of six years.

questions.q: Article 48A, which relates to the protection and improvement of the environment and safeguarding of forests and wildlife, was added by:
questions.e: Article 48A was added to the Constitution by the 42nd Amendment Act of 1976.

questions.q: With reference to the 'Directives Outside Part IV', consider the following: 1️⃣ Claims of SCs and STs to Services (Article 335). 2️⃣ Instruction in mother tongue at primary stage (Article 350-A). 3️⃣ Development of the Hindi Language (Article 351).
questions.e: All three are directives found in other parts of the Constitution besides Part IV. Article 335 is in Part XVI, while Articles 350-A and 351 are in Part XVII.

questions.q: In which famous case did the Supreme Court rule that "the Indian Constitution is founded on the bedrock of the balance between the Fundamental Rights and the Directive Principles"?
questions.e: In the Minerva Mills case (1980), the Supreme Court emphasized the balance between Part III (Fundamental Rights) and Part IV (Directive Principles).

questions.q: Consider the following statements about the implementation of DPSP: 1️⃣ The Planning Commission was established in 1950 to facilitate development in a planned manner. 2️⃣ The Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972 was enacted to implement the directive regarding forests and wildlife. 3️⃣ The Criminal Procedure Code (1973) separated the judiciary from the executive in public services.
questions.e: All statements are correct implementations of DPSP. The Planning Commission (now NITI Aayog) facilitates economic goals , the Wildlife Act (1972) supports Article 48A , and the CrPC (1973) fulfilled Article 50 regarding the separation of judiciary from executive.

questions.q: Which of the following statements regarding the Prime Minister of India is correct? 1️⃣ The Constitution provides a specific procedure for the selection and appointment of the Prime Minister. 2️⃣ Article 75 says only that the Prime Minister shall be appointed by the President. 3️⃣ The President has no individual discretion in the appointment of the Prime Minister.
questions.e: Statement 2 is correct as Article 75 only states that the PM shall be appointed by the President. Statement 1 is incorrect because the Constitution does not contain any specific procedure. Statement 3 is incorrect because the President can exercise individual discretion when no party has a clear majority in the Lok Sabha.

questions.q: In 1980, the Delhi High Court (and later the Supreme Court) held that:
o: The Constitution does not require that a person must prove his majority in the Lok Sabha before he is appointed as the Prime Minister.
The Prime Minister can only be from the Lok Sabha.
The Prime Minister must prove his majority in the Lok Sabha before being appointed.
A person must be a member of either House of Parliament before being appointed Prime Minister.
questions.e: The Delhi High Court ruled that the Constitution does not require a person to prove a majority before appointment; the President can appoint a PM and then ask them to prove the majority within a reasonable period.

questions.q: With reference to the membership of the Prime Minister in Parliament, consider the following: 1️⃣ A person who is not a member of either House of Parliament can be appointed as Prime Minister for six months. 2️⃣ Constitutionally, the Prime Minister may be a member of any of the two Houses of Parliament. 3️⃣ In Britain, the Prime Minister should definitely be a member of the Lower House (House of Commons).
questions.e: All statements are correct. A non-member can be PM for 6 months. The PM can be from the Lok Sabha or Rajya Sabha in India. In Britain, by convention, the PM must be from the House of Commons.

questions.q: Which of the following are the powers and functions of the Prime Minister in relation to the Council of Ministers? 1️⃣ He recommends persons who can be appointed as ministers by the President. 2️⃣ He allocates and reshuffles various portfolios among the ministers. 3️⃣ He can ask a minister to resign or advise the President to dismiss him. 4️⃣ His resignation or death automatically dissolves the council of ministers.
questions.e: All these are powers of the PM. As the head of the council, his resignation or death leads to the collapse of the entire ministry.

questions.q: The Prime Minister serves as the chairman of which of the following bodies? 1️⃣ NITI Aayog 2️⃣ National Integration Council 3️⃣ Inter-State Council 4️⃣ National Water Resources Council
questions.e: The Prime Minister is the ex-officio chairman of all these bodies.

questions.q: With reference to Article 78, which of the following is a duty of the Prime Minister?
o: To communicate to the President all decisions of the council of ministers relating to the administration of the affairs of the Union.
To advise the President on the removal of the Comptroller and Auditor General.
To preside over the joint sitting of Parliament.
To appoint the Attorney General of India.
questions.e: Article 78 specifies the PM's duty to communicate all decisions of the council of ministers to the President.

questions.q: Consider the following statements regarding the President's power in relation to the Council of Ministers: 1️⃣ The President may require the Prime Minister to submit for consideration of the council any matter on which a decision has been taken by a minister but which has not been considered by the council. 2️⃣ The President is bound to act according to the advice of the Council of Ministers. 3️⃣ This binding nature of advice was added by the 42nd and 44th Amendment Acts.
questions.e: All statements are correct. Article 78(c) allows the President to refer a minister's decision to the full council. Articles 74 and 75, as amended by the 42nd and 44th Amendments, make the council's advice binding on the President.

questions.q: Who among the following Prime Ministers headed a 'caretaker' government?
questions.e: Charan Singh headed a caretaker government in 1979 after the President dissolved the Lok Sabha following his resignation before proving a majority.

questions.q: Regarding the appointment of ministers, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ They are appointed by the President on the advice of the Prime Minister. 2️⃣ A minister who is not a member of Parliament for any period of six consecutive months shall cease to be a minister. 3️⃣ The salaries and allowances of ministers are determined by the President.
questions.e: Statement 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect because the salaries and allowances of ministers are determined by Parliament, not the President.

questions.q: What is the maximum strength of the Council of Ministers, including the Prime Minister, as per the 91st Amendment Act, 2003?
o: 10% of the total strength of the Lok Sabha.
20% of the total strength of the Lok Sabha.
15% of the total strength of the Lok Sabha.
questions.e: The 91st Amendment Act of 2003 mandated that the total number of ministers, including the PM, shall not exceed 15% of the total strength of the Lok Sabha.

questions.q: The Principle of 'Collective Responsibility' implies that: 1️⃣ The Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha. 2️⃣ All ministers own joint responsibility to the Lok Sabha for all their acts of omission and commission. 3️⃣ When the Lok Sabha passes a no-confidence motion against the council, all ministers must resign, including those from the Rajya Sabha.
questions.e: Collective responsibility is a fundamental principle of the parliamentary system, codified in Article 75, meaning the council acts as a single team and is responsible to the Lok Sabha.

questions.q: Consider the following statements regarding 'Individual Responsibility': 1️⃣ It is contained in Article 75. 2️⃣ It means that the ministers hold office during the pleasure of the President. 3️⃣ The President can remove a minister even at a time when the council of ministers enjoys the confidence of the Lok Sabha, but only on the advice of the PM.
questions.e: All statements are correct. Article 75 states ministers hold office during the pleasure of the President, which in practice means the PM can ensure their removal by advising the President.

questions.q: Which of the following statements is/are correct regarding the 'Legal Responsibility' of ministers in India? 1️⃣ There is no provision in the Constitution for the system of legal responsibility of a minister. 2️⃣ An order of the President for a public act must be counter-signed by a minister. 3️⃣ Courts are barred from inquiring into the nature of advice rendered by ministers to the President.
questions.e: Statement 1 and 3 are correct. India does not have the British system where ministers must countersign royal orders. Article 74(2) bars courts from inquiring into the advice given by ministers to the President.

questions.q: The 'Cabinet' differs from the 'Council of Ministers' in which of the following ways? 1️⃣ The Cabinet is a smaller body consisting of 15 to 20 ministers. 2️⃣ The Council of Ministers is a constitutional body, whereas the Cabinet was not mentioned in the original text of the Constitution. 3️⃣ The Cabinet meets as a body to take decisions, while the Council of Ministers does not.
questions.e: All statements are correct. The Cabinet is the inner core of the Council of Ministers. The word 'Cabinet' was added to Article 352 by the 44th Amendment in 1978 and was not in the original text.

questions.q: With reference to 'Cabinet Committees', consider the following statements: 1️⃣ They are extra-constitutional in emergence. 2️⃣ They are of two types—standing and ad hoc. 3️⃣ They are usually chaired by the Prime Minister. 4️⃣ Their membership is restricted only to Cabinet Ministers.
questions.e: Statements 1, 2, and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is incorrect because while they usually include cabinet ministers, non-cabinet ministers can also be members.

questions.q: Which of the following Cabinet Committees is NOT chaired by the Prime Minister?
questions.e: The Parliamentary Affairs Committee is chaired by the Home Minister.

questions.q: The "Super-Cabinet" is a term often used to describe which committee?
questions.e: The Political Affairs Committee is often described as a "Super-Cabinet" as it deals with all policy matters pertaining to domestic and foreign affairs.

questions.q: Consider the following statements about the Attorney General of India: 1️⃣ He is the highest law officer in the country. 2️⃣ He must be a person who is qualified to be appointed a judge of the Supreme Court. 3️⃣ His term of office is fixed by the Constitution as five years.
questions.e: Statement 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect because the Constitution does not fix his term; he holds office during the pleasure of the President.

questions.q: With reference to the 'Kitchen Cabinet' in India, consider the following: 1️⃣ It is a formal constitutional body. 2️⃣ It consists of the Prime Minister and two to four influential colleagues. 3️⃣ It can include outsiders like friends or family members of the Prime Minister.
questions.e: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. The 'Kitchen Cabinet' or 'Inner Cabinet' is an informal, extra-constitutional body where the PM discusses important matters.

questions.q: Under Article 74, there shall be a Council of Ministers with the Prime Minister at the head to aid and advise the President. The Supreme Court in 1971 and 1974 held that:
o: The Council of Ministers does not cease to exist even after the dissolution of the Lok Sabha.
The Prime Minister can act independently of the council.
The President can act without the aid and advice of the council during a session of Parliament.
The advice of the council is optional for the President.
questions.e: The Supreme Court ruled that even after the dissolution of the Lok Sabha, the Council of Ministers does not cease to exist, and the President cannot exercise executive power without their aid and advice.

questions.q: Which of the following Articles deals with the conduct of business of the Government of India?
questions.e: Article 77 deals with the conduct of business, specifying that all executive actions of the Government of India shall be expressed to be taken in the name of the President.

questions.q: Regarding the 'Caretaker Government', which of the following statements is/are correct? 1️⃣ The President can appoint a person as Prime Minister and ask him to prove his majority later. 2️⃣ A caretaker government is expected to take significant new policy decisions. 3️⃣ The normal channel of accountability through Parliament does not exist for a caretaker government.
questions.e: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is incorrect because caretaker governments are constrained from taking significant new policy decisions or major spending.

questions.q: In the context of "Parliamentary Affairs Committee", who is its current chairman as per the text?
questions.e: The Cabinet Committee on Parliamentary Affairs is chaired by the Home Minister.

questions.q: Which of the following is/are the functions of the "Economic Affairs Committee"? 1️⃣ To direct and coordinate government activities in the economic sphere. 2️⃣ To deal with all policy matters pertaining to foreign affairs. 3️⃣ To decide on the appointments to the three armed forces.
questions.e: Statement 1 is the primary function of the Economic Affairs Committee. Foreign affairs are handled by the Political Affairs Committee, and high-level appointments are handled by the Appointments Committee.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ The Council of Ministers is a constitutional body. 2️⃣ The Cabinet is an informal body with no mention in the Constitution. 3️⃣ The 44th Amendment Act introduced the definition of Cabinet in Article 352.
questions.e: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. The Council of Ministers is provided in Articles 74 and 75. Statement 2 is incorrect because the Cabinet was given constitutional status and defined in Article 352 by the 44th Amendment.

questions.q: Which Prime Minister headed the first minority government in India?
questions.e: V.P. Singh headed the first minority government (National Front) in 1989.

questions.q: With reference to "Shadow Cabinet", consider the following: 1️⃣ It is a unique institution of the British cabinet system. 2️⃣ It is formed by the opposition party to balance the ruling cabinet. 3️⃣ There is no such institution in India.
questions.e: All statements are correct. The Shadow Cabinet is a British institution where opposition members "shadow" ministers to prepare for office; India does not have this.

questions.q: Which of the following Articles was added by the 42nd Amendment Act to the DPSP? 1️⃣ Article 39A (Free legal aid). 2️⃣ Article 43A (Participation of workers in management). 3️⃣ Article 43B (Promotion of co-operative societies). 4️⃣ Article 48A (Protection of environment).
questions.e: Articles 39A, 43A, and 48A were added by the 42nd Amendment. Article 43B was added by the 97th Amendment in 2011.

questions.q: "The state shall endeavour to secure for the citizens a uniform civil code" is mentioned under:
questions.e: This is the explicit provision of Article 44.

questions.q: Which Article of the DPSP deals with the "Separation of judiciary from executive"?
questions.e: Article 50 directs the State to take steps to separate the judiciary from the executive in the public services.

questions.q: The "National Integration Council" is chaired by:
questions.e: The Prime Minister is the chairman of the National Integration Council.

questions.q: Consider the following statements about the Prime Minister's office: 1️⃣ He is the principal channel of communication between the President and the Council of Ministers. 2️⃣ He advises the President with regard to the appointment of important officials like the CAG and CEC. 3️⃣ He can recommend dissolution of the Lok Sabha to the President at any time.
questions.e: All these are critical constitutional and political functions of the Prime Minister.

questions.q: "Living wage, etc., for workers" is a directive under:
questions.e: Article 43 directs the State to secure a living wage and a decent standard of life for all workers.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a Liberal-Intellectual Principle?
questions.e: Promotion of cottage industries is a Gandhian Principle, not a Liberal-Intellectual one.

questions.q: The 44th Amendment Act (1978) added one Directive Principle to Article 38, which is:
o: Free legal aid to the poor.
Minimize inequalities in income, status, facilities, and opportunities.
questions.e: The 44th Amendment Act added a directive to Article 38 to minimize inequalities in income and status.

questions.q: With reference to the 'Instrument of Instructions' under the Government of India Act of 1935, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ They were issued to the Governors and the Governor-General by the British Government. 2️⃣ The Directive Principles of State Policy are merely another name for these instructions. 3️⃣ The only difference is that DPSPs are instructions to the legislature and the executive.
questions.e: The Directive Principles resemble the 'Instrument of Instructions' enumerated in the Government of India Act of 1935. They are constitutional instructions to the State in legislative, executive, and administrative matters. As Dr. B.R. Ambedkar stated, DPSPs are like the Instrument of Instructions, but they are addressed to the executive and legislature.

questions.q: Which of the following statements is/are correct regarding the 'Non-justiciable' nature of Directive Principles? 1️⃣ They are not legally enforceable by the courts for their violation. 2️⃣ The Constitution makes them fundamental in the governance of the country. 3️⃣ It is the moral obligation of the State authorities to apply them in making laws.
questions.e: Directive Principles are non-justiciable, meaning they are not legally enforceable by courts. However, Article 37 declares that these principles are fundamental in the governance of the country and it shall be the duty of the State to apply them in making laws. They impose a moral obligation on state authorities.

questions.q: Consider the following statements about the classification of Directive Principles: 1️⃣ Socialistic Principles aim at providing social and economic justice. 2️⃣ Gandhian Principles are based on the programme of reconstruction during the national movement. 3️⃣ Liberal-Intellectual Principles represent the ideology of liberalism.
questions.e: The principles are classified into three broad categories: Socialistic, which aim at social and economic justice; Gandhian, based on the national movement's reconstruction programme; and Liberal-Intellectual, reflecting liberalism.

questions.q: Which of the following Socialistic Directive Principles is/are correct? 1️⃣ Article 39: To secure the right to adequate means of livelihood for all citizens. 2️⃣ Article 41: To secure the right to work, education, and public assistance in certain cases. 3️⃣ Article 42: To make provision for just and humane conditions of work and maternity relief.
questions.e: These are all Socialistic principles: Article 39 focuses on livelihood, Article 41 on the right to work and education, and Article 42 on humane work conditions and maternity relief.

questions.q: Regarding the 'Gandhian Principles', which of the following is/are explicitly mentioned in the DPSP? 1️⃣ To organize village panchayats (Article 40). 2️⃣ To promote cottage industries in rural areas (Article 43). 3️⃣ To promote the educational and economic interests of SCs, STs, and other weaker sections (Article 46).
questions.e: All these are Gandhian principles: Article 40 for village panchayats, Article 43 for cottage industries, and Article 46 for the interests of SCs, STs, and weaker sections.

questions.q: Consider the following statements regarding 'Liberal-Intellectual' principles: 1️⃣ Article 44: Uniform Civil Code for the citizens. 2️⃣ Article 50: Separation of judiciary from executive in public services. 3️⃣ Article 51: Promotion of international peace and security.
questions.e: These fall under the Liberal-Intellectual category: Article 44 for a Uniform Civil Code, Article 50 for separating judiciary and executive, and Article 51 for international peace.

questions.q: Which of the following Directive Principles were added by the 42nd Amendment Act of 1976? 1️⃣ Article 39: To secure opportunities for healthy development of children. 2️⃣ Article 39A: To promote equal justice and provide free legal aid to the poor. 3️⃣ Article 43A: To take steps to secure the participation of workers in management. 4️⃣ Article 48A: To protect and improve the environment.
questions.e: The 42nd Amendment Act of 1976 added four new Directive Principles: Article 39 (opportunities for children), Article 39A (free legal aid), Article 43A (workers' participation), and Article 48A (environment protection).

questions.q: With reference to the 'Conflict between Fundamental Rights and Directive Principles', consider the following: 1️⃣ In the Champakam Dorairajan case, the SC ruled that DPSPs are subsidiary to Fundamental Rights. 2️⃣ The 25th Amendment Act gave primacy to Articles 39(b) and 39(c) over Articles 14, 19, and 31. 3️⃣ In the Minerva Mills case, the SC declared that DPSPs have absolute primacy over all Fundamental Rights.
questions.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: the SC initially made DPSPs subsidiary, and the 25th Amendment gave primacy to Article 39(b) and (c). Statement 3 is incorrect because the Minerva Mills case struck down the provision giving DPSPs primacy over all FRs, emphasizing a balance instead.

questions.q: Which Constitutional Amendment Act made a provision for the State to provide early childhood care and education for all children until they complete the age of six years?
questions.e: The 86th Amendment Act of 2002 changed the subject matter of Article 45, making elementary education a fundamental right (Article 21A), while the new Article 45 directs the State to provide early childhood care and education up to age six.

questions.q: Consider the following statements about the 'Sanctions' behind DPSP: 1️⃣ The real force behind them is political (public opinion). 2️⃣ Sir B.N. Rau recommended that the rights of an individual should be divided into justiciable and non-justiciable. 3️⃣ They are intended to be the 'basis of all future legislation' in the country.
questions.e: The DPSP's primary sanction is the moral force of public opinion. The classification into justiciable and non-justiciable was recommended by Sir B.N. Rau. The Constituent Assembly intended them to be the basis of future governance.

questions.q: Regarding the 'Prime Minister' of India, which of the following statements is/are correct? 1️⃣ He is the head of the State. 2️⃣ He is the head of the Government. 3️⃣ The Constitution requires that he must be a member of the Lok Sabha at the time of appointment.
questions.e: The Prime Minister is the head of the Government, while the President is the head of the State. Statement 3 is incorrect because a person who is not a member of either House can be appointed PM for six months.

questions.q: With reference to the appointment of the Prime Minister, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ When no party has a clear majority, the President may exercise personal discretion. 2️⃣ The President usually appoints the leader of the largest party or coalition as the PM. 3️⃣ The PM must prove his majority in the Lok Sabha before taking the oath of office.
questions.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct regarding the President's discretionary power in a "hung Parliament". Statement 3 is incorrect; the SC has ruled the President can appoint a PM and then ask them to prove the majority within a reasonable period.

questions.q: Consider the following regarding the Prime Minister’s powers in relation to the Council of Ministers: 1️⃣ He advises the President on the appointment of other ministers. 2️⃣ He can dismiss a minister directly without advising the President. 3️⃣ His resignation or death leads to the automatic dissolution of the council of ministers.
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct as the President appoints ministers only on PM's advice. Statement 2 is incorrect; the PM advises the President to dismiss a minister. Statement 3 is correct; since the PM is the head, his exit collapses the entire council.

questions.q: Which of the following is/are the duties of the Prime Minister as per Article 78? 1️⃣ To communicate all decisions of the council of ministers to the President. 2️⃣ To furnish such information relating to the administration of the affairs of the Union as the President may call for. 3️⃣ To submit for consideration of the council any matter on which a decision has been taken by a minister but not considered by the council, if the President so requires.
questions.e: All three points are explicitly listed as the PM's duties towards the President under Article 78.

questions.q: With reference to the 'Central Council of Ministers', consider the following statements: 1️⃣ Article 74 deals with the status of the council. 2️⃣ Article 75 deals with the appointment, tenure, and responsibility of ministers. 3️⃣ The council of ministers is collectively responsible to the Parliament.
questions.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect; according to Article 75, the council of ministers is collectively responsible specifically to the Lok Sabha (the House of the People), not the entire Parliament.

questions.q: Under Article 74, the advice tendered by the Council of Ministers to the President: 1️⃣ Shall be inquired into by any court. 2️⃣ Is binding on the President after the 42nd and 44th Amendment Acts. 3️⃣ The President may require the council to reconsider such advice.
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect; Article 74(2) states that the advice shall not be inquired into by any court. Statements 2 and 3 are correct: the 42nd Amendment made the advice binding, and the 44th Amendment added that the President can ask for reconsideration, but must act on the subsequent advice.

questions.q: What is the maximum strength of the Union Council of Ministers as per the 91st Amendment Act, 2003?
o: 10% of the total strength of Lok Sabha.
15% of the total strength of Lok Sabha.
10% of the total strength of Parliament.
15% of the total strength of Parliament.
questions.e: The 91st Amendment Act of 2003 provided that the total number of ministers, including the PM, in the Central Council of Ministers shall not exceed 15% of the total strength of the Lok Sabha.

questions.q: Consider the following statements regarding the 'Collective Responsibility' of ministers: 1️⃣ It is the fundamental principle of the parliamentary system. 2️⃣ All ministers own joint responsibility to the Lok Sabha for all their acts of omission and commission. 3️⃣ A no-confidence motion passed against the council requires all ministers, including those from Rajya Sabha, to resign.
questions.e: Collective responsibility means the council acts as a team. If the Lok Sabha passes a no-confidence motion, the entire ministry must resign, regardless of which House individual ministers belong to.

questions.q: With reference to the 'Individual Responsibility' of ministers, which of the following is/are correct? 1️⃣ Article 75 contains the principle of individual responsibility. 2️⃣ It means that the ministers hold office during the pleasure of the President. 3️⃣ The President can remove a minister only on the advice of the Prime Minister.
questions.e: All statements are correct. Article 75 states ministers hold office during the President's pleasure. In practice, the PM can ask for a minister's resignation or advise the President to dismiss them.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes the 'Legal Responsibility' of ministers in India?
o: The Constitution of India does not provide for a system of legal responsibility of a minister.
Courts can inquire into the legal advice given by ministers.
Every order of the President for a public act must be countersigned by a minister.
Ministers are legally responsible for every public act of the President.
questions.e: Unlike Britain, where ministers must countersign royal orders and are legally responsible, India has no such provision. The courts are also barred from inquiring into the advice given to the President.

questions.q: Consider the following statements regarding the 'Cabinet': 1️⃣ It is a smaller body consisting of 15 to 20 ministers. 2️⃣ It was not mentioned in the original text of the Constitution. 3️⃣ It was inserted in Article 352 by the 44th Amendment Act of 1978.
questions.e: All statements are correct. The Cabinet is the inner core of the Council of Ministers. The word was added to the Constitution via the 44th Amendment to define it as the Council consisting of the PM and other Ministers of Cabinet rank.

questions.q: What is the "Super-Cabinet" according to the text?
questions.e: The Political Affairs Committee is often described as a "Super-Cabinet" because it deals with all policy matters pertaining to domestic and foreign affairs.

questions.q: Regarding 'Cabinet Committees', consider the following statements: 1️⃣ They are extra-constitutional in emergence. 2️⃣ They are of two types: standing and ad hoc. 3️⃣ They are always chaired by the Prime Minister.
questions.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect; while the PM chairs most, some are chaired by other ministers, such as the Parliamentary Affairs Committee which is chaired by the Home Minister.

questions.q: Which of the following is/are the roles of the 'Cabinet'? 1️⃣ It is the highest decision-making authority in our politico-administrative system. 2️⃣ It is the supreme direction-controlling body of the Central government. 3️⃣ it is the chief policy-formulating body of the Central government.
questions.e: The Cabinet performs all these roles as the top-tier executive body.

questions.q: With reference to the 'Kitchen Cabinet', which of the following is/are correct? 1️⃣ It is a formal constitutional body. 2️⃣ It consists of the PM and two to four influential colleagues. 3️⃣ It can include outsiders like family members or friends of the Prime Minister.
questions.e: The Kitchen Cabinet is an informal, extra-constitutional body. It usually consists of a few close colleagues and may sometimes include personal friends or family.

questions.q: Consider the following statements regarding the "Shadow Cabinet": 1️⃣ It is a unique institution of the British cabinet system. 2️⃣ It is formed by the opposition party to prepare its members for future ministerial office. 3️⃣ There is no such institution in India.
questions.e: All statements are correct. The Shadow Cabinet is a British concept where opposition members "shadow" actual ministers; it does not exist in the Indian system.

questions.q: Which of the following Directive Principles are based on 'Liberal-Intellectual' ideology? 1️⃣ To secure a uniform civil code for all citizens (Article 44). 2️⃣ To provide early childhood care and education for all children (Article 45). 3️⃣ To separate the judiciary from the executive (Article 50). 4️⃣ To promote cottage industries (Article 43).
questions.e: Articles 44, 45, and 50 are Liberal-Intellectual. Article 43 (cottage industries) is a Gandhian principle.

questions.q: According to Article 39(f), the State shall direct its policy towards securing:
o: That children are given opportunities and facilities to develop in a healthy manner.
questions.e: Article 39(f) specifically directs the state to secure opportunities for the healthy development of children.

questions.q: With reference to the 'Directives Outside Part IV', Article 351 deals with:
o: Claims of SCs and STs to services.
Instruction in mother tongue at primary stage.
questions.e: Article 351, located in Part XVII, directs the Union to promote the spread of the Hindi language.

questions.q: In which case did the Supreme Court hold that "Fundamental Rights are not sacrosanct and can be amended by the Parliament"?
questions.e: In the Kesavananda Bharati case (1973), the SC overruled the Golak Nath case and held that Parliament can amend any part of the Constitution, including FRs, as long as it doesn't damage the basic structure.

questions.q: Which of the following statements regarding the "Board of Control" is/are correct? 1️⃣ It was created by Pitt’s India Act of 1784 to manage political affairs. 2️⃣ It was empowered to supervise all operations of the civil and military government of the British possessions. 3️⃣ It was abolished by the Government of India Act of 1858.
questions.e: All statements are correct. The Board of Control was established in 1784, given supervisory powers over civil/military government, and abolished in 1858 when the office of Secretary of State was created.

questions.q: With reference to the 'Regulating Act of 1773', which of the following is correct?
o: It provided for the establishment of a Federal Court.
It made the Governors of Bombay and Madras independent of Bengal.
It designated the Governor of Bengal as 'Governor-General of Bengal'.
It abolished the Court of Directors.
questions.e: The Act designated the Governor of Bengal as the 'Governor-General of Bengal'. It made the other presidencies subordinate to Bengal.

questions.q: Consider the following regarding the 'Charter Act of 1833': 1️⃣ It was the final step towards centralisation in British India. 2️⃣ It made Lord William Bentick the first Governor-General of India. 3️⃣ It deprived the Governors of Bombay and Madras of their legislative powers.
questions.e: All statements are correct. This act was the final step in centralisation, appointed Bentick as the first GG of India, and centralized legislative powers in the GG of India.

questions.q: The 'Macaulay Committee' (1854) was related to which of the following?
questions.e: The Macaulay Committee was the Committee on the Indian Civil Service, appointed in 1854 following the Charter Act of 1853.

questions.q: With reference to the 'Government of India Act of 1858', which of the following is/are correct? 1️⃣ It changed the designation of Governor-General of India to Viceroy of India. 2️⃣ Lord Canning became the first Viceroy. 3️⃣ It created a 15-member Council of India to assist the Secretary of State.
questions.e: All statements are correct features of the 1858 Act, which established the Crown Rule.

questions.q: Which Act introduced the system of 'communal representation' for Muslims for the first time?
questions.e: The Indian Councils Act of 1909, also known as Morley-Minto Reforms, introduced separate electorates for Muslims.

questions.q: Regarding the 'Government of India Act of 1919', consider the following statements: 1️⃣ It introduced bicameralism and direct elections for the first time. 2️⃣ It divided provincial subjects into transferred and reserved. 3️⃣ It provided for the establishment of a Central Public Service Commission.
questions.e: All statements are correct. The Act introduced bicameralism, provincial dyarchy, and led to the setup of a Public Service Commission in 1926.

questions.q: Which of the following features belong to the 'Government of India Act of 1935'? 1️⃣ Establishment of an All-India Federation. 2️⃣ Abolition of dyarchy in the provinces. 3️⃣ Establishment of the Reserve Bank of India. 4️⃣ Creation of a Federal Court.
questions.e: All these were major provisions of the lengthy 1935 Act.

questions.q: The 'Poona Pact' (1932) was an agreement between:
o: Muslim League and the British Government.
questions.e: The Poona Pact was an agreement between the Congress and Dr. B.R. Ambedkar to retain the Hindu joint electorate while giving reserved seats to the depressed classes.

questions.q: Consider the following statements regarding the 'Indian Independence Act of 1947': 1️⃣ It declared India as an independent and sovereign state from August 15, 1947. 2️⃣ It abolished the office of Viceroy. 3️⃣ It proclaimed the lapse of British paramountcy over Indian princely states.
questions.e: All these were key features of the 1947 Act that ended British rule.

questions.q: Who was the Chairman of the 'Union Constitution Committee'?
questions.e: Jawaharlal Nehru was the chairman of both the Union Powers Committee and the Union Constitution Committee.

questions.q: Which of the following is/are 'Minor Committees' of the Constituent Assembly? 1️⃣ Credentials Committee 2️⃣ House Committee 3️⃣ Order of Business Committee 4️⃣ Steering Committee
questions.e: Steering Committee was a Major Committee. The others listed (Credentials, House, Order of Business) were Minor Committees.

questions.q: Consider the following statements regarding the 'Drafting Committee': 1️⃣ It was set up on August 29, 1947. 2️⃣ It consisted of seven members. 3️⃣ N. Madhava Rau replaced B.L. Mitter who resigned due to ill-health.
questions.e: All statements are correct. The committee was chaired by Dr. Ambedkar and included members like N. Madhava Rau.

questions.q: On which date was the Constitution of India 'Adopted, Enacted and Given to themselves' by the people?
questions.e: November 26, 1949, is the date of adoption as mentioned in the Preamble.

questions.q: Which Article of the Constitution deals with the "Authoritative text in Hindi language"?
questions.e: Article 394A was inserted by the 58th Amendment Act of 1987 to provide for an authoritative text of the Constitution in Hindi.

questions.q: Which of the following statements regarding the 'Fundamental Rights' (Part III) and 'Directive Principles' (Part IV) is/are correct? 1️⃣ The Fundamental Rights are justiciable, whereas the Directive Principles are non-justiciable. 2️⃣ The Directive Principles require legislation for their implementation, whereas most Fundamental Rights are self-executory. 3️⃣ The Courts are bound to declare a law as void if it is inconsistent with any Directive Principle.
questions.e: Fundamental Rights are justiciable and mostly self-executory. Directive Principles are non-justiciable and require legislation for implementation. Statement 3 is incorrect because courts cannot void a law solely for being inconsistent with a DPSP, though they can for Fundamental Rights under Article 13.

questions.q: With reference to Article 39, which of the following is/are 'Socialistic' directives? 1️⃣ The operation of the economic system does not result in the concentration of wealth. 2️⃣ Equal pay for equal work for both men and women. 3️⃣ Promotion of cottage industries on an individual or co-operative basis in rural areas.
questions.e: Article 39(c) and (d) are socialistic principles focusing on wealth distribution and equal pay. Promotion of cottage industries (Article 43) is a Gandhian principle.

questions.q: Consider the following statements about the 'Prime Minister' as a channel of communication: 1️⃣ It is the duty of the PM to communicate to the President all decisions of the Council of Ministers. 2️⃣ The PM must furnish information relating to administration as the President may call for. 3️⃣ The President cannot refer a decision taken by an individual minister to the Council without the PM's consent.
questions.e: Under Article 78, the PM is the principal channel of communication between the President and the Council. Statement 3 is incorrect because Article 78(c) empowers the President to require the PM to submit a minister's decision to the Council for consideration.

questions.q: Which of the following Cabinet Committees is often described as the "Super-Cabinet"?
questions.e: The Political Affairs Committee deals with all policy matters pertaining to domestic and foreign affairs and is thus described as a "Super-Cabinet".

questions.q: Regarding the 'Individual Responsibility' of ministers under Article 75: 1️⃣ Ministers hold office during the pleasure of the President. 2️⃣ The President can remove a minister only on the advice of the Prime Minister. 3️⃣ It ensures that the PM can exercise power over his colleagues.
questions.e: Article 75 incorporates individual responsibility where ministers hold office during the President's pleasure, and the President removes them only on the PM's advice, effectively giving the PM control over the team.

questions.q: Which of the following was added to the DPSP by the 44th Amendment Act, 1978?
o: Minimize inequalities in income, status, facilities, and opportunities.
Free legal aid to the poor.
Participation of workers in management of industries.
questions.e: The 44th Amendment Act added Article 38(2), directing the State to minimize inequalities in income, status, facilities, and opportunities.

questions.q: With reference to the 'Cabinet', consider the following: 1️⃣ It is a constitutional body mentioned in Article 74. 2️⃣ Its role is advisory to the President and its advice is generally binding. 3️⃣ It is the supreme direction-controlling body of the Central government.
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect because 'Cabinet' was not in the original text; it was inserted into Article 352 by the 44th Amendment. Statements 2 and 3 correctly describe its advisory role and supreme status.

questions.q: Which of the following acts as the "Guardian of the Public Purse"?
questions.e: The Comptroller and Auditor-General (CAG) is an independent body that audits accounts and acts as the guardian of the public purse.

questions.q: Under the "Collective Responsibility" principle, if the Lok Sabha passes a no-confidence motion:
o: Only the ministers from the Lok Sabha must resign.
The entire Council of Ministers must resign.
Only the Prime Minister must resign.
questions.e: Collective responsibility means all ministers own joint responsibility; a no-confidence motion requires the entire Council of Ministers to resign, including those from the Rajya Sabha.

questions.q: Which Article directs the State to "separate the judiciary from the executive in the public services"?
questions.e: Article 50, a Liberal-Intellectual principle, directs the State to separate the judiciary from the executive in public services.

questions.q: Regarding the "Kitchen Cabinet" in the Indian system: 1️⃣ It is an extra-constitutional body. 2️⃣ It consists of the PM and 2-4 influential colleagues. 3️⃣ It may include outsiders like friends or family.
questions.e: The 'Kitchen Cabinet' or 'Inner Cabinet' is an informal, extra-constitutional body consisting of the PM and a few close associates, potentially including non-ministers.

questions.q: Which of the following is correct about 'Article 31-C' as an exception to Fundamental Rights?
o: It gives primacy to all DPSPs over all Fundamental Rights.
It protects laws giving effect to Article 39(b) and (c) from Articles 14 and 19.
It protects all laws from being challenged in court.
It was part of the original Constitution.
questions.e: Article 31-C, added by the 25th Amendment, provides that laws implementing the socialistic principles in Article 39(b) and (c) cannot be voided for violating Articles 14 or 19.

questions.q: The "Instrument of Instructions" (1935 Act) is similar to:
questions.e: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar stated that Directive Principles are like the 'Instrument of Instructions' issued to Governors under the 1935 Act.

questions.q: Which Prime Minister headed the first minority government in India that depended on outside support?
questions.e: V.P. Singh headed the National Front government in 1989, which was the first minority government in India.

questions.q: In the context of "Cabinet Committees", who chairs the "Appointments Committee"?
questions.e: The Appointments Committee of the Cabinet is chaired by the Prime Minister.

questions.q: Which of the following is a 'Gandhian' principle in the DPSP?
o: Free legal aid to the poor
questions.e: Article 40, which directs the state to organize village panchayats, is a Gandhian principle.

questions.q: Consider the following statements about the "Council of Ministers" and "Cabinet": 1️⃣ The Council of Ministers is a larger body (60-70 ministers). 2️⃣ The Cabinet is a part of the Council of Ministers. 3️⃣ The Council of Ministers meets frequently to take decisions.
questions.e: The Council is a large body, while the Cabinet is a smaller inner core. Statement 3 is incorrect because the Council of Ministers as a whole rarely meets; the Cabinet meets frequently to take decisions.

questions.q: Which Constitutional Amendment Act added "Promotion of co-operative societies" to the DPSP?
questions.e: The 97th Amendment Act of 2011 added Article 43-B to the Directive Principles.

questions.q: Under Article 74, the President may require the Council of Ministers to reconsider their advice: 1️⃣ Only once. 2️⃣ The President must act in accordance with the advice tendered after such reconsideration. 3️⃣ This provision was added by the 42nd Amendment Act.
questions.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect because this 'reconsideration' provision was added by the 44th Amendment Act, 1978, while the 42nd Amendment originally made the advice absolute.

questions.q: Which Article directs the State to "protect and improve the environment"?
questions.e: Article 48A, added by the 42nd Amendment, directs the state to protect and improve the environment and safeguard forests and wildlife.

questions.q: Regarding the "Shadow Cabinet" in Britain: 1️⃣ It is formed by the ruling party. 2️⃣ It helps in specialized knowledge and efficiency. 3️⃣ Indian system does not have this institution.
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect; the Shadow Cabinet is formed by the *Opposition*. Statements 2 and 3 are correct.

questions.q: Which of the following are functions of the "Political Affairs Committee"? 1️⃣ Deals with domestic and foreign affairs. 2️⃣ Chaired by the Prime Minister. 3️⃣ Deals with economic activities.
questions.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Economic activities are handled by the Economic Affairs Committee.

questions.q: According to Article 37, the Directive Principles are fundamental in:
questions.e: Article 37 explicitly states that these principles are fundamental in the governance of the country.

questions.q: Who was the Prime Minister of the first coalition government in India?
questions.e: Morarji Desai headed the first non-Congress coalition government in 1977.

questions.q: "To promote equal justice and to provide free legal aid to the poor" is the provision of:
questions.e: This is the specific provision of Article 39A, added by the 42nd Amendment.

questions.q: With reference to the "Legal Responsibility" of ministers in Britain: 1️⃣ Every order of the King for a public act must be countersigned by a minister. 2️⃣ The King can do no wrong. 3️⃣ There is no legal responsibility of ministers in India.
questions.e: All statements are correct; Britain follows the countersignature and "King can do no wrong" principles, whereas India has no legal responsibility system.

questions.q: Which Article directs the state to "organize agriculture and animal husbandry on modern and scientific lines"?
questions.e: Article 48 directs the state to organize agriculture and animal husbandry on modern and scientific lines.

questions.q: Regarding the appointment of the PM, if the incumbent PM dies suddenly:
o: The President may appoint a new PM in his individual discretion.
The Lok Sabha is automatically dissolved.
The President must wait for the party to elect a leader.
questions.e: If an incumbent PM dies suddenly and there is no clear successor, the President can exercise individual discretion in appointing a new PM.

questions.q: Which Directive Principle was added by the 97th Amendment Act, 2011?
questions.e: The 97th Amendment added Article 43-B regarding co-operative societies.

questions.q: "Collective Responsibility" of the Council of Ministers is provided in:
questions.e: Article 75 explicitly states that the Council of Ministers shall be collectively responsible to the House of the People.

questions.q: Which Cabinet Committee is chaired by the Home Minister?
questions.e: The Parliamentary Affairs Committee is chaired by the Home Minister.

questions.q: "To promote international peace and security" is a directive under:
questions.e: Article 51 directs the state to promote international peace and security.

questions.q: Regarding the nature of the PM's advice to the President: 1️⃣ It is confidential. 2️⃣ It can be challenged in court if it violates laws. 3️⃣ Article 74(2) bars judicial inquiry into the advice.
questions.e: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is incorrect; Article 74(2) states that the advice tendered by Ministers to the President shall not be inquired into by any court.

questions.q: Which Directive Principle emphasizes "Right to work, to education and to public assistance"?
questions.e: Article 41 directs the state to secure the right to work, education, and public assistance in certain cases.

questions.q: The word "Cabinet" was defined in the Constitution by:
questions.e: The 44th Amendment Act (1978) added the definition of Cabinet to Article 352.

questions.q: Who was the first Prime Minister to resign from office?
questions.e: Morarji Desai was the first PM to resign from office after losing the support of his party.

questions.q: The "Appointments Committee of the Cabinet" deals with: 1️⃣ Higher level appointments in the Central Secretariat. 2️⃣ Appointments to the Public Enterprises. 3️⃣ Appointments to the Banks and Financial Institutions.
questions.e: This committee handles high-level appointments across these sectors.

questions.q: "Provision for just and humane conditions of work and maternity relief" is under:
questions.e: This is the directive of Article 42.

questions.q: Regarding the membership of the Council of Ministers: 1️⃣ They must be members of either House. 2️⃣ A non-member can stay as a minister for up to 6 months. 3️⃣ They have the right to vote in both Houses.
questions.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect; a minister can speak in both Houses but can only vote in the House of which they are a member.

questions.q: Which Directive Principle targets "equal pay for equal work"?
questions.e: Article 39(d) directs the state to secure equal pay for equal work for both men and women.

questions.q: The "Cabinet" is an advisory body to the:
questions.e: The Cabinet aids and advises the President in the exercise of his functions.

questions.q: Which case established that "Fundamental Rights and Directive Principles are two wheels of a chariot"?
questions.e: The Minerva Mills case (1980) emphasized the balance and harmony between the two.

questions.q: "To separate the judiciary from the executive" is a:
questions.e: Article 50 is classified as a Liberal-Intellectual principle.

questions.q: Who among the following became PM without having been a member of either House at the time of appointment? 1️⃣ H.D. Deve Gowda 2️⃣ P.V. Narasimha Rao 3️⃣ Manmohan Singh
questions.e: P.V. Narasimha Rao (1991) and H.D. Deve Gowda (1996) were not members of either House when appointed PM.

questions.q: "To secure for all citizens a Uniform Civil Code" is under:
questions.e: This is provided in Article 44.

questions.q: The "Economic Affairs Committee" is chaired by:
questions.e: The Prime Minister chairs the Economic Affairs Committee.

questions.q: Regarding "Individual Responsibility", the PM can:
questions.e: Under individual responsibility, the PM can ask a minister to resign or advise the President to dismiss them.

questions.q: "To promote the educational and economic interests of SCs and STs" is:
questions.e: This is the provision of Article 46.

questions.q: Which Article describes the duties of the Prime Minister towards the President?
questions.e: Article 78 lists the PM's duties to furnish information and communicate decisions.

questions.q: The 42nd Amendment Act added how many new DPSPs?
questions.e: The 42nd Amendment added four new Directive Principles: 39(f), 39A, 43A, and 48A.

questions.q: Which of the following statements is/are correct regarding the 'Union of India' and 'Territory of India'? 1️⃣ The 'Territory of India' is a wider expression than the 'Union of India'. 2️⃣ The 'Union of India' includes only the States. 3️⃣ The 'Territory of India' includes States, Union Territories, and territories that may be acquired.
questions.e: The 'Territory of India' is a wider expression because the 'Union of India' includes only the states, while the former includes states, UTs, and any acquired territories. States are members of the federal system, whereas UTs are directly administered by the Centre.

questions.q: Consider the following regarding Article 3 of the Constitution: 1️⃣ Parliament can form a new state by uniting a part of any state to any other state. 2️⃣ A bill for this purpose can be introduced only with the prior recommendation of the President. 3️⃣ The President must refer the bill to the state legislature for its binding opinion.
questions.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct as per Article 3. Statement 3 is incorrect because while the President must refer the bill for views, the opinion of the state legislature is not binding on the President or Parliament.

questions.q: With reference to the 'Berubari Union' case (1960), the Supreme Court held that:
o: Article 3 includes the power to diminish the area of India as a whole.
Indian territory can be ceded to a foreign state only by amending the Constitution under Article 368.
Parliament can cede Indian territory to a foreign country under Article 3.
Settlement of boundary disputes always requires a constitutional amendment.
questions.e: The Supreme Court held that the power of Parliament to diminish the area of a state under Article 3 does not cover the cession of Indian territory to a foreign country; such action requires a constitutional amendment under Article 368.

questions.q: Regarding the 'Evolution of States', which commission first recommended the reorganization of states on a linguistic basis?
questions.e: While the Dhar Commission and JVP Committee rejected the linguistic basis, the Fazl Ali Commission (States Reorganisation Commission, 1953) broadly accepted language as the basis of reorganization.

questions.q: Which of the following pairs of 'State - Year of Creation' is NOT correctly matched?
questions.e: Nagaland was formed in 1963 by taking the Naga Hills and Tuensang area out of Assam. Gujarat was created in 1960, Haryana in 1966, and Sikkim became a full state in 1975.

questions.q: With reference to 'Citizenship' (Articles 5-11), consider the following: 1️⃣ Article 5 deals with citizenship at the commencement of the Constitution. 2️⃣ Article 9 states that persons voluntarily acquiring foreign citizenship shall not be Indian citizens. 3️⃣ Article 11 empowers the Parliament to regulate the right of citizenship by law.
questions.e: All statements are correct. Article 5 identifies citizens at the start, Article 9 prohibits dual citizenship, and Article 11 gives Parliament plenary power over citizenship matters.

questions.q: Under the Citizenship Act, 1955, a person born in India on or after July 1, 1987, is a citizen only if:
o: His/her birth is registered at an Indian consulate.
Either of his/her parents is a citizen of India at the time of birth.
He/she is ordinarily resident for five years.
questions.e: For those born between July 1, 1987, and December 3, 2004, the law requires that at least one parent must be an Indian citizen at the time of birth.

questions.q: A person can acquire Indian citizenship by 'Naturalisation' if he/she: 1️⃣ Is not a citizen of a country that prevents Indians from becoming citizens. 2️⃣ Has an adequate knowledge of a language specified in the Eighth Schedule. 3️⃣ Has resided in India for at least 14 years in total.
questions.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct qualifications. Statement 3 is slightly incorrect; the applicant must have resided in India for 11 years out of the 14 years preceding the 12-month period before the application.

questions.q: Consider the following regarding the 'Loss of Citizenship': 1️⃣ Renunciation is a voluntary act. 2️⃣ Termination occurs automatically if a person knowingly acquires foreign citizenship. 3️⃣ Deprivation is a compulsory termination by the Central Government based on fraud or disloyalty.
questions.e: The Citizenship Act (1955) prescribes these three ways: renunciation (voluntary), termination (automatic on acquiring another citizenship), and deprivation (compulsory for fraud, disloyalty, etc.).

questions.q: Which of the following rights are conferred on citizens of India but denied to aliens? 1️⃣ Right against discrimination on grounds of religion, race, etc. (Article 15). 2️⃣ Right to equality of opportunity in public employment (Article 16). 3️⃣ Protection of life and personal liberty (Article 21).
questions.e: Articles 15 and 16 are available only to citizens. Article 21 (Life and Liberty) is available to both citizens and foreigners (except enemy aliens).

questions.q: With reference to 'Article 12', which of the following falls under the definition of 'State'? 1️⃣ Local authorities like municipalities and panchayats. 2️⃣ Statutory bodies like ONGC and SAIL. 3️⃣ Private bodies working as an instrument of the State.
questions.e: Article 12 includes all legislative and executive organs, all local authorities, and other statutory/non-statutory authorities. The SC also ruled that private bodies acting as state instruments fall under this definition.

questions.q: According to the 'Rule of Law' propounded by A.V. Dicey, which element is NOT applicable to the Indian System?
o: The Constitution is the result of the rights of the individual.
questions.e: In India, the first two elements apply, but the third does not; in India, the Constitution is the *source* of individual rights, rather than the rights being the source of the Constitution as in the British system.

questions.q: Consider the following statements about Article 14: 1️⃣ It permits 'class legislation' but forbids 'reasonable classification'. 2️⃣ Classification must be based on an intelligible differentia. 3️⃣ The 'Rule of Law' is a basic feature of the Constitution.
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect; Article 14 *forbids* class legislation but *permits* reasonable classification. Statements 2 and 3 are correct.

questions.q: Which of the following is/are an exception to the rule of equality (Article 14)? 1️⃣ The President of India is not answerable to any court for his official acts. 2️⃣ No criminal proceedings can be instituted against a Governor during his term. 3️⃣ Foreign ambassadors enjoy immunity from civil and criminal proceedings.
questions.e: All are correct exceptions. Article 361 provides immunities to the President and Governors, and international law grants immunity to diplomats.

questions.q: Article 15(2) prohibits discrimination regarding access to shops and use of wells by:
o: Both the State and private individuals.
Neither, it is only a directive.
questions.e: Article 15(2) says no citizen shall be subject to disability regarding public places on grounds of religion, race, etc.; this prohibits discrimination by both the State and private persons.

questions.q: Which Constitutional Amendment Act added Article 15(5) regarding reservation for OBCs in educational institutions?
questions.e: The 93rd Amendment Act of 2005 empowered the state to make special provisions for socially/educationally backward classes in admissions to educational institutions, including private ones.

questions.q: Consider the following regarding Article 16: 1️⃣ It provides equality of opportunity for all citizens in public employment. 2️⃣ Parliament can prescribe residence as a requirement for certain posts. 3️⃣ The State can make provisions for reservation of appointments in favor of any backward class.
questions.e: All statements are correct. Article 16(1) provides equality, 16(3) allows residence requirements via Parliament, and 16(4) allows reservations for under-represented backward classes.

questions.q: The 'Mandal Commission' (1979) was appointed to investigate the conditions of:
questions.e: The Morarji Desai Government appointed the Second Backward Classes Commission under B.P. Mandal under Article 340 to investigate the conditions of socially/educationally backward classes.

questions.q: In the Indra Sawhney case (1992), the Supreme Court ruled that: 1️⃣ Total reserved quota should not exceed 50%. 2️⃣ The 'creamy layer' must be excluded from OBC benefits. 3️⃣ Reservation should be provided in both appointments and promotions.
questions.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect because the SC ruled that reservation should be confined to initial appointments and not promotions.

questions.q: Which Constitutional Amendment Act empowered the state to provide 10% reservation to EWSs in public employment?
questions.e: The 103rd Amendment Act of 2019 added Article 16(6), enabling reservation of up to 10% for economically weaker sections in appointments.

questions.q: Consider the following regarding Article 17: 1️⃣ It abolishes 'untouchability' and forbids its practice. 2️⃣ It is available only against the State. 3️⃣ The term 'untouchability' is defined in the Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955.
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is incorrect as the right is available against private individuals too. Statement 3 is incorrect because the term is not defined in either the Constitution or the Act.

questions.q: Article 18 prohibits the State from conferring titles, but allows which of the following?
o: Titles from foreign states without President's consent.
questions.e: Article 18 prohibits titles but exempts military or academic distinctions.

questions.q: With reference to the 'Six Rights' under Article 19, consider the following: 1️⃣ They are protected against both state and private action. 2️⃣ They are available only to citizens. 3️⃣ The State can impose 'reasonable' restrictions on them.
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect; they are protected *only* against state action. Statements 2 and 3 are correct.

questions.q: The 'Freedom of Speech and Expression' includes which of the following? 1️⃣ Freedom of the press. 2️⃣ Right against tapping of telephonic conversations. 3️⃣ Right to strike.
questions.e: The SC has held that Article 19 includes freedom of the press and the right against phone tapping. However, it does *not* include the right to strike.

questions.q: Article 20 provides protection in respect of conviction for offences. It includes: 1️⃣ No ex-post-facto law. 2️⃣ No double jeopardy. 3️⃣ No self-incrimination.
questions.e: All three are specific protections under Article 20.

questions.q: Consider the following regarding the 'Right to Life' (Article 21): 1️⃣ In the Gopalan case, the SC took a narrow interpretation. 2️⃣ In the Maneka case, the SC took a wider interpretation. 3️⃣ It includes the right to marry a person of one's choice.
questions.e: All statements are correct. The SC moved from a narrow view in 1950 to a wider "due process" view in 1978. It has since declared the right to marry a person of one's choice as part of Article 21.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a right declared as part of Article 21?
o: Right to get a government job
questions.e: The SC has included privacy, shelter, and travel abroad under Article 21, but there is no fundamental right to a government job.

questions.q: Article 22 grants protection to persons who are arrested or detained. Which type of detention is based on 'suspicion' without trial and conviction?
questions.e: Preventive detention is a precautionary measure based on suspicion, whereas punitive detention occurs after a trial and conviction.

questions.q: According to Article 22, the detention of a person under preventive detention cannot exceed ______ unless an advisory board reports sufficient cause.
questions.e: The Constitution provides that preventive detention cannot exceed three months without advisory board approval.

questions.q: Article 23 prohibits which of the following? 1️⃣ Traffic in human beings. 2️⃣ Begar (forced labour). 3️⃣ Compulsory service for public purposes without discrimination.
questions.e: Statements 1 and 2 are prohibited. Statement 3 is an *exception* where the state *can* impose service for public purposes.

questions.q: Under Article 24, employment of children below 14 years is prohibited in: 1️⃣ Factories. 2️⃣ Mines. 3️⃣ Harmless or innocent work.
questions.e: Article 24 prohibits employment in factories, mines, or hazardous work, but does not prohibit harmless or innocent work.

questions.q: Which of the following is correct regarding 'Freedom of Religion' (Article 25)? 1️⃣ It includes the right to convert another person. 2️⃣ It is subject to public order, morality, and health. 3️⃣ It covers both religious beliefs and religious practices.
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect; it does not include a right to convert, as forcible conversion impinges on another's freedom of conscience. Statements 2 and 3 are correct.

questions.q: Article 26 grants rights to 'religious denominations' to: 1️⃣ Establish and maintain institutions for religious purposes. 2️⃣ Manage its own affairs in matters of religion. 3️⃣ Own and acquire movable and immovable property.
questions.e: All these rights are explicitly granted to religious denominations under Article 26.

questions.q: Article 27 prevents the State from:
o: Spending public money collected via tax for the promotion of any particular religion.
questions.e: Article 27 states that no person shall be compelled to pay taxes for the promotion or maintenance of any specific religion. It prohibits tax use but not the levy of fees.

questions.q: Regarding Article 28, in which type of educational institution is religious instruction completely prohibited?
o: Institutions administered by the State but established under an endowment.
Institutions receiving aid from the State.
Institutions wholly maintained by the State.
questions.e: Religious instruction is strictly prohibited in institutions 100% maintained out of State funds.

questions.q: Consider the following regarding Article 29: 1️⃣ It protects the right of any section of citizens to conserve their distinct language. 2️⃣ It protects only religious and linguistic minorities. 3️⃣ It includes the right to agitate for the protection of a language.
questions.e: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is incorrect; the SC held it includes both minorities and the majority.

questions.q: Under Article 30, minorities have the right to: 1️⃣ Establish and administer educational institutions of their choice. 2️⃣ Impart education to their children in their own language. 3️⃣ Not be discriminated against in matters of state aid.
questions.e: All these are rights granted to religious and linguistic minorities under Article 30.

questions.q: Which Article was described by Dr. Ambedkar as "the heart and soul of the Constitution"?
questions.e: Dr. Ambedkar called Article 32 the most important article, without which the Constitution would be a nullity.

questions.q: With reference to the 'Writ Jurisdiction', which of the following is correct? 1️⃣ Only the Supreme Court can issue writs. 2️⃣ The Supreme Court's jurisdiction is original but not exclusive. 3️⃣ High Courts can issue writs for purposes other than the enforcement of Fundamental Rights.
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect; High Courts also issue writs under Article 226. Statements 2 and 3 are correct.

questions.q: The writ of 'Habeas Corpus' literally means:
questions.e: Habeas Corpus is a Latin term meaning 'to have the body of'.

questions.q: Which writ is issued by a higher court to a lower court to *quash* an order already passed?
questions.e: Certiorari is issued to quash an order based on excess or lack of jurisdiction, whereas Prohibition is issued *before* the final order to stop the proceeding.

questions.q: The writ of 'Quo-Warranto' can be sought by:
questions.e: Unlike other writs, Quo-Warranto can be sought by any person, not necessarily the one whose rights were directly violated.

questions.q: Consider the following regarding Article 33: 1️⃣ It empowers the Parliament to restrict FRs of the armed forces. 2️⃣ It also covers non-combatants like cooks and barbers in the forces. 3️⃣ Laws made under it can be challenged for violating Fundamental Rights.
questions.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect; such laws cannot be challenged on FR grounds.

questions.q: 'Martial Law' differs from 'National Emergency' because:
o: National Emergency suspends the government and ordinary law courts.
Martial Law affects only Centre-State relations.
Martial Law is imposed to restore order due to any reason, whereas National Emergency has specific grounds.
National Emergency is imposed only in specific areas.
questions.e: Martial Law is imposed for breakdown of order and suspends ordinary courts/government. National Emergency continues them and is limited to three grounds (war, aggression, rebellion).

questions.q: According to Article 35, the power to make laws for prescribing punishment for offences against Fundamental Rights vests in:
questions.e: Article 35 ensures uniformity across India by vesting this power solely in the Parliament.

questions.q: Which Article was added to protect land reform laws from judicial review?
questions.e: Article 31B along with the Ninth Schedule was added by the 1st Amendment (1951) to protect specific laws from being invalidated on FR grounds.

questions.q: With reference to Article 31C, consider the following: 1️⃣ It was inserted by the 25th Amendment Act. 2️⃣ It protects laws implementing Directive Principles in Article 39(b) and (c). 3️⃣ It provides that such laws cannot be challenged for violating Articles 14 or 19.
questions.e: All statements are correct. Article 31C gives primacy to specific socialistic DPSPs over specific Fundamental Rights.

questions.q: Which case established that "Judicial Review" is a basic feature of the Constitution?
questions.e: In the Minerva Mills case (1980), the SC struck down the 42nd Amendment's attempt to exclude judicial review, holding it as a basic feature.

questions.q: The 'Directive Principles of State Policy' are described by Dr. Ambedkar as:
questions.e: Dr. Ambedkar described the Directive Principles as 'novel features' of the Indian Constitution.

questions.q: According to the 'Minerva Mills' case, the Indian Constitution is founded on the balance between:
o: The Prime Minister and the President.
questions.e: The Supreme Court held that the Constitution is built on the bedrock of the balance between Part III (Fundamental Rights) and Part IV (Directive Principles).

questions.q: Which of the following is correct regarding Article 36?
o: It lists the duties of the Prime Minister.
It describes the powers of the Cabinet.
It defines 'State' for the purposes of Part IV.
questions.e: Article 36 states that the term 'State' in Part IV has the same meaning as in Part III dealing with Fundamental Rights.

questions.q: With reference to Socialistic Principles in Part IV, consider the following: 1️⃣ Article 38 aims to promote the welfare of the people. 2️⃣ Article 41 secures the right to work and education. 3️⃣ Article 43 aims to secure a living wage for workers.
questions.e: All these are socialistic directives aimed at achieving social and economic justice.

questions.q: Which Gandhian principle directs the state to "organize village panchayats"?
questions.e: Article 40 directs the state to organize village panchayats and endow them with necessary powers.

questions.q: Article 44, regarding a Uniform Civil Code, is classified as a:
questions.e: The Uniform Civil Code (Article 44) represents the ideology of liberalism and falls under the Liberal-Intellectual category.

questions.q: Which Article directs the state to "protect monuments and places of national importance"?
questions.e: Article 49 directs the state to protect every monument or place of artistic or historic interest declared to be of national importance.

questions.q: Consider the following regarding the Prime Minister: 1️⃣ He is appointed by the President. 2️⃣ He chooses his ministers and the President appoints them on his advice. 3️⃣ He can be a member of either House of Parliament.
questions.e: All statements are correct. Article 75 mandates appointment by the President. The PM chooses the team and can belong to Lok Sabha or Rajya Sabha.

questions.q: In 1997, the Supreme Court ruled that a person who is not a member of either House can be appointed as a Minister for a period of:
questions.e: A person can be a minister (including PM) for six consecutive months without being a member of Parliament, after which they must be elected or cease to hold office.

questions.q: The Prime Minister is the ex-officio chairman of: 1️⃣ NITI Aayog. 2️⃣ National Integration Council. 3️⃣ Inter-State Council.
questions.e: The PM chairs all these important national bodies.

questions.q: Regarding the 'Central Council of Ministers', which of the following is correct? 1️⃣ The total number of ministers cannot exceed 15% of the Lok Sabha strength. 2️⃣ They hold office during the pleasure of the President. 3️⃣ They are collectively responsible to the Rajya Sabha.
questions.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect; they are collectively responsible specifically to the Lok Sabha.

questions.q: Which Cabinet Committee deals with all policy matters pertaining to domestic and foreign affairs?
questions.e: The Political Affairs Committee is the most powerful committee, often called the "Super-Cabinet".

questions.q: Who among the following became Prime Minister of India without ever being a member of either House during their tenure?
