questions.e: While Rao and Deve Gowda were not members *at the time of appointment*, they both became members within the mandatory six-month period. No one can remain PM beyond six months without being a member.

questions.q: With reference to 'Cabinet Committees', consider the following: 1️⃣ They are extra-constitutional. 2️⃣ They are set up by the Prime Minister. 3️⃣ Their membership can include non-cabinet ministers.
questions.e: All statements are correct. They are not in the Constitution, are formed by the PM according to needs, and can include ministers of state.

questions.q: The 'Shadow Cabinet' is a feature of:
questions.e: The Shadow Cabinet is a unique British institution where the opposition forms a parallel cabinet to track actual ministers.

questions.q: Which Article deals with the 'Conduct of Business' of the Government of India?
questions.e: Article 77 specifies that all executive actions shall be taken in the name of the President and provides for the allocation of business among ministers.

questions.q: According to Article 78, who is the principal channel of communication between the President and the Council of Ministers?
questions.e: It is the duty of the PM to keep the President informed about all decisions and administrative affairs.

questions.q: Which Constitutional Amendment Act added the word 'Cabinet' to the Constitution?
questions.e: The 44th Amendment Act of 1978 inserted the word 'Cabinet' into Article 352.

questions.q: Under Article 74, the advice of the Council of Ministers is:
o: Inquired into by the Supreme Court.
questions.e: The 42nd and 44th Amendments made the council's advice binding, though the President can ask for one-time reconsideration.

questions.q: The 'Collective Responsibility' of ministers means: 1️⃣ They are jointly responsible to the Lok Sabha. 2️⃣ They must defend all cabinet decisions even if they personally disagree. 3️⃣ If a minister disagrees with a cabinet decision and is not prepared to defend it, he must resign.
questions.e: All statements are correct. Collective responsibility requires a unified front; disagreement necessitates resignation.

questions.q: Which of the following describes the 'Kitchen Cabinet'?
o: The group of ministers in charge of food and supplies.
An informal body of the PM and 2-4 influential associates.
A committee dealing with internal security.
A formal body established by Article 75.
questions.e: The Kitchen Cabinet is a small, informal circle of advisors where real power often resides.

questions.q: The 'Appointments Committee' of the Cabinet is chaired by:
questions.e: The PM chairs this committee, which handles all high-level appointments in the central government.

questions.q: Regarding 'Legal Responsibility' of ministers, India follows:
o: The concept that 'the King can do no wrong'.
No provision for legal responsibility of a minister.
The British model of countersigning orders.
The American model of ministerial liability.
questions.e: In India, there is no requirement for ministers to countersign President's orders, and thus no legal responsibility system exists.

questions.q: Which Prime Minister of India headed the first non-Congress government?
questions.e: Morarji Desai led the Janata Party government in 1977.

questions.q: Which Article of the DPSP was added by the 97th Amendment Act, 2011?
questions.e: Article 43B, regarding the promotion of co-operative societies, was added by the 97th Amendment.

questions.q: The 'Separation of Judiciary from Executive' (Article 50) is a:
questions.e: Article 50 is part of the Liberal-Intellectual classification.

questions.q: Who described the Fundamental Rights and Directive Principles as the 'Conscience of the Constitution'?
questions.e: Granville Austin used this term for the two parts together.

questions.q: Which of the following is correct about the Prime Minister's role in the House? 1️⃣ He is the leader of the Lower House. 2️⃣ He can recommend the dissolution of the Lok Sabha to the President at any time. 3️⃣ He announces government policies on the floor of the House.
questions.e: All these are powers of the PM as the leader of the House.

questions.q: The 'Economic Affairs Committee' deals with:
o: Directing and coordinating government activities in the economic sphere.
The appointment of the RBI Governor.
questions.e: This committee oversees all major economic policy issues.

questions.q: 'Individual Responsibility' under Article 75 means:
o: Ministers hold office during the pleasure of the President.
The PM is responsible for each minister's actions.
Each minister is responsible to the Parliament individually.
The President can dismiss the PM at any time.
questions.e: It means the President can remove a minister even if the council has majority, but only on PM's advice.

questions.q: Which Directive Principle directs the state to "promote international peace and security"?
questions.e: Article 51 focuses on international relations and world peace.

questions.q: The 'Council of Ministers' is a:
questions.e: The Council is a large body (60-70 ministers), while the Cabinet is a small inner core (15-20 ministers).

questions.q: Which meeting of the GST Council introduced the revised two-rate structure?
questions.e: The 56th GST Council meeting rationalized the rates into 5% and 18%.

questions.q: The 'Nowcasting' model integrates which of the following?
questions.e: These high-frequency indicators are used for real-time growth assessment.

questions.q: Which Act redesignated 'Governor-General of India' as 'Viceroy of India'?
questions.e: The 1858 Act changed the designation to Viceroy, who was the direct representative of the Crown.

questions.q: The 'Account Aggregator' framework handles:
o: Financial data sharing based on consent.
questions.e: It allows individuals to share their financial footprints securely for credit appraisal.

questions.q: Which Article prohibits 'Begar' and forced labor?
questions.e: Article 23 prohibits traffic in human beings and all forms of forced labor.

questions.q: 'Viksit Bharat' targets achieved by:
questions.e: 2047 is the target year for India's centenary of independence.

questions.q: Which Article is the 'Magna Carta' of India?
questions.e: Part III (Fundamental Rights) is described as the Magna Carta of India.

questions.q: The 'Creamy Layer' among OBCs includes:
questions.e: The government excludes high-ranking officials and professionals from OBC reservation.

questions.q: 'Mission LiFE' was introduced to nudge:
questions.e: It promotes mindful utilization instead of mindless consumption.

questions.q: Which Fundamental Right protects minorities' right to establish educational institutions?
questions.e: Article 30 gives all religious and linguistic minorities the right to run their own institutions.

questions.q: The 'Critical Minerals Mission' targets minerals like:
questions.e: These minerals are vital for EV batteries and green tech.

questions.q: Which writ is the 'bulwark of individual liberty'?
questions.e: It protects against arbitrary or illegal detention.

questions.q: 'SASCI' loans provided to states are:
questions.e: They are interest-free 50-year loans for capital investment.

questions.q: Which Act introduced 'Separate Electorates' for Muslims?
questions.e: The Morley-Minto Reforms introduced communal representation for Muslims.

questions.q: 'PM-JANMAN' addresses the needs of:
questions.e: It targets socio-economic development for vulnerable tribal groups.

questions.q: Which Article empowers Parliament to change state boundaries?
questions.e: Article 3 allows Parliament to redraw the political map of India.

questions.q: 'BharatNet' connects administrative units at:
questions.e: It connects villages with high-speed optical fiber.

questions.q: Which Fundamental Right guarantees 'protection of life'?
questions.e: Article 21 declares no person shall be deprived of life or liberty except by legal procedure.

questions.q: The 'Economic Complexity Index' (ECI) rank of India in 2022:
questions.e: India's rank improved from 54 in 2012 to 42 in 2022.

questions.q: The 'Viksit Bharat Shiksha Adhishthan Bill' deals with:
questions.e: It seeks to grant total autonomy to top-tier universities to reach global rankings.
